question: Does the applicability of the MUTCD to a facility open to public travel depend on whether the facility is publicly or privately owned or on the source of its funding?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The MUTCD's applicability to a facility open to public travel does not depend on whether the facility is publicly or privately owned, nor on its funding source. The controlling factor is whether the facility is open to public travel; the Manual applies to both public and private streets, roadways, bikeways, and toll roads open to the public, and it explicitly does not apply to certain facilities (such as gated private roadways restricted at all times) regardless of ownership. Standards (mandatory): - "In accordance with 23 CFR 655.603(a), the MUTCD shall apply to all of the following types of facilities: A. Any street, roadway, or bikeway open to public travel, either publicly or privately owned; B. Streets and roadways on sites that are off the public right-of-way that are open to public travel without full-time access restrictions... C. Publicly-owned toll roads, including those under the jurisdiction of a public agency, public authority, or public-private partnership; D. Privately-owned toll roads where the public is allowed to travel without access restriction... and E. Grade crossings of publicly-owned roadways with railroads or light rail transit." - "The MUTCD shall not apply to the following types of facilities: A. Roadways within private gated properties where access to the general public is restricted at all times; B. Grade crossings of privately-owned roadways with railroads; and C. Parking areas, including the driving aisles within those parking areas, that are either publicly or privately owned." Citations: - Section 1A.01 Support §5 (p.1) - Section 1B.01 Standard §2 (p.4) - Section 1B.01 Standard §3 (p.4) Note: Section 1A.01 Support §5 states this principle directly — "The applicability of the MUTCD to facilities open to public travel is independent of the type of ownership or jurisdiction (public or private) and the source of funding (Federal, State, local, or private)" — but as a Support provision it is explanatory rather than normative; the binding requirements are the Standard provisions quoted above.
gold_answer: No. Applicability is independent of public or private ownership or jurisdiction and independent of whether funding is Federal, State, local, or private.
